newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Unknown firm buys 9.32 pct of Russia's Uralmash.
newsitem.headline: Unknown firm buys 9.32 pct of Russia's Uralmash.

text.p: Unknown Yekaterinburg-based firm TOO Skela bought 9.32 percent of shares in one of Russia's biggest machine-builders, AO Uralmash, at a Thursday auction for 41.44 billion roubles ($7.2 million), a local property fund chairman said.
Viktor Basargin told Reuters he could not say who Skela's founders were.

He said the government had put 335,991 shares up for sale in a cash auction, each with a face value of 500 roubles. The actual sale price was 123,338 roubles per share with a starting price of 10,000 roubles.
Cyprus's Regent Pacific Nominas offered the second biggest sum for the shares -- 32.91 billion roubles.
"If within 50 days Skela does not pay 41.44 billion roubles for Uralmash shares, Cyprus's Regent Pacific Nominas will be the winner," Basargin said.
Uralmash's authorised capital is 1.8 billion roubles. Its preferred shares account for 22 percent of total capital.
Bioprotsess owns 30 percent of the company, Uralmash's management owns 18 percent, 12 percent is owned by companies and nine percent by individuals.
